The correction strengthens the unit (the appointed-time word frames 11:29-11:35) and it bears on the neighbouring edge at 11:28/11:29, since the same clause closes 11:27.

items.claim: The edge at 12:8/12:9 parts a question from its answer. 12:8 does not end on the seer's failure to understand; its second half is his question to the man (words 5-9), and 12:9 is the reply. The row declines a cut at 12:6/12:7 because it would split a question from the oath that answers it, then accepts the same kind of split at 12:8/12:9. What supports the edge is the PE after 12:8 (one witness) and a change of speaker introduced by a plain and-he-said, which is a weak connective. The rival that keeps the pairs whole, 12:5-12:13 as one unit of nine verses, is within the size target and was declined on that mark; a second rival, an edge at 12:7/12:8, was not weighed at all.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed by this lane; the seam goes to the end review as mark-led. At 12:8/12:9: close side, 12:8 words 1-4 answer the oath just heard (the hearing verb of 12:7 word 1 returns at 12:8 word 2), but words 5-9 open a new exchange with a question; onset side, 12:9 opens with and-he-said and the reply, with no formula of its own; a PE follows 12:8. At the unweighed rival 12:7/12:8: close side, the oath ends on the finishing of all these things; onset side, 12:8 opens with the fronted first-person pronoun, and its question ends on the same demonstrative; against it, the hearing verb binds 12:8 back to 12:7 and the PE stands one verse later. 12:8 faces both ways, so neither edge is clean.

suggested_fix.fact: 12:8 ends with the seer's question and 12:9 answers it, so an edge at 12:8/12:9 divides a question from its answer and rests on the PE after 12:8 (one witness) with a weak connective; the rivals to weigh are 12:5-12:13 as one unit of nine verses and an edge at 12:7/12:8, where 12:8 opens with the fronted first-person pronoun.
